tinygo: The host must call the exported `_initialize` before any other export (the WASI reactor convention); Go's `init()` and the runtime start there. True of every probe, so it is not a cost on any one feature.
kotlin: The host must run `_start` (the WASI command convention) before any other export; true of every module that built. Feature 17 (`externref`) is built for the `wasm-js` target, every other probe for `wasm-wasi`.

27.note: Zig defines an `exception_handling` target feature and LLVM has a direct `llvm.wasm.throw(tag, ptr)` intrinsic (used by libc++abi's `__cxa_throw`) callable the same way as the lead for 26. Zig's error-union model never generates that IR for its own control flow, so there is no path from ordinary Zig code to this machinery; only raw module-level assembly writing `try_table`/`throw_ref` text directly could reach it, which is speculative given the same assembler-directive bugs in 18/19/10 (zig#13165).

04.note: Same root cause as 03: no table-emitting code path exists in Kotlin's own codegen at all (`WasmTable` is decoder-only), so table import/export has nothing to produce.

flags: Pointer API over a zero-page memory
06.note: `kotlin.wasm.unsafe.MemoryAllocator.allocate()` only hands back runtime-assigned addresses from a bump allocator; there is no API to place data at a caller-chosen fixed address. Static data (string literals/arrays) goes through passive segments feeding GC arrays (see 13), not user-controlled linear-memory offsets.

07.note: Confirmed via source: the compiler's custom-section writer (`AnnotationKind` in `WasmIrToBinary.kt`) supports only three hardcoded, `private`, internal section kinds (`metadata.code.branch_hint`, `metadata.code.trace_inst`, a JS-called marker). No generic name+bytes custom-section API is exposed anywhere.

10.note: Lead: source inspection (`DeclarationGenerator.generateField`) shows every top-level Kotlin property DOES compile to a real mutable Wasm global, not a GC-heap field — the premise holds. But no public annotation exports/imports a property's global directly; the only global-export code path found (`multimoduleExportIfNeeded`) is scoped to class vtables under the internal `-Xwasm-generate-closed-world-multimodule` flag. Worth testing whether that flag/mechanism can be repurposed for a plain top-level var before treating this as confirmed.

12.note: `ByteArray.fill/copyInto` become `array.fill` / `array.copy`. Confirmed via source: `memory.fill`/`memory.copy` have zero emission sites in the ir2wasm backend (the opcodes exist only in the generic decoder table); ByteArray ops stay on GC arrays.

13.note: Kotlin keeps string literals in passive data segments of its own; the program cannot request one, and has no linear memory to copy it into. Confirmed via source: passive segments are wired only to `array.new_data` feeding GC arrays; `memory.init` has zero emission sites in the backend.
